## 3. The evidence that moved it

**The pretrained component is removed, and the method still works.**
[39384986](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39384986/) (*Nat Methods*): de novo protein design with a denoising
diffusion network **independent of pretrained structure-prediction models**. The
foundation-model thread's claim is that scale and pretraining produce
transferable general-purpose models. A title announcing independence from
pretraining as the contribution is the cleanest available refutation of that
claim, and it is a constructive one — the ablation is the result.

**A generalist biomedical vision-language model.** [39112796](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39112796/) (*Nat Med*)
runs in the other direction in the same month. November 2024 has both the
generalist claim and its ablation.

**[39546375](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39546375/): an agent pointed at a working scientist's own data.** LmRaC
lets an LLM interrogate user experimental results. The agentic thread's claim is
about research *infrastructure* rather than demonstrations, and a tool that takes
a user's own unpublished results as input is infrastructure by that definition.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

The diffusion-without-pretraining paper above is filed on `foundation-models`, and
it is one of six refutations on tracked threads this month. Two more land on the
same thread, and both are about deployment rather than about models:
[39122964](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39122964/) (*Nat Med*) — in a
randomised double-blind trial, deep-learning embryo selection in IVF failed to
meet non-inferiority against manual morphology, which is a prospective negative
for a deployed clinical AI rather than a benchmark result; and
[39054373](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39054373/) (*Nat Med*) — identical
medical advice was rated worse when patients were told AI was involved, a barrier
to deployment that no improvement in accuracy touches. With the generalist
vision–language model in section 3, `foundation-models` closes +2 / −3.

[39348147](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39348147/) (*JAMA*) — a pragmatic
randomised trial of *Helicobacter pylori* screening to prevent gastric cancer was
null in intention-to-treat. `interception`'s claim is that acting on the precursor
changes the outcome, and this is that claim tested at population scale and not
supported. [39562005](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39562005/) (*JITC*) — a
B7-H3-targeting nanobody CAR-T shows on-target off-tumour toxicity that
antigen-sensitivity tuning only partly avoids.

[39385035](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39385035/) (*Nature*) is the odd one:
adding CTLA-4 blockade abrogates the resistance to PD-(L)1 inhibition associated
with KEAP1/STK11 alterations. It is carded against `immunotherapy-resistance`
because genotype-defined resistance turns out not to be fixed — which is a good
result for patients and a refutation of the thread's premise at the same time.

### (b) Method credibility

November 2024 takes twenty cards here, +3 / −17, against November 2025's
seventeen. Across the corpus this thread's largest month is January 2024 at
thirty. The 2024 monthly counts run between five and thirty with a median of
14.5; the 2025 counts run between nine and twenty-two with a median of sixteen.
Those two distributions are not distinguishable by eye or by any reading this
corpus supports. So the visible difference between November 2024 and November
2025 in *this file* is mostly a difference in how hard each month was read, which
is the error the whole corpus has been correcting for.

Three of the twenty are supports, which on a thread reading `crisis` is worth
naming: applying the competing WHO and ICC lymphoma classifications to real-world
cases changes assignment in under 1% of them
[39255410](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39255410/) (*Blood*); the Stockholm3
prostate risk score validates prospectively in a multiethnic cohort, beyond the
population it was trained on [39038251](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39038251/)
(*JCO*); and the HLH-2004 diagnostic criteria, re-examined against real cases,
perform as intended [39046779](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39046779/)
(*Blood*). That is the most passes this ledger has recorded in a single month up
to this point.
